Name: 16_patient_doctors_lover_faithful
Representative_Docs:
['1. Why does the Jizera so sadly murmur, a road winds around it, along which a young man walks thoughtful, his heart is very pained.  
2. Gradually he stops, takes paper and pencil out of his pocket, begins to write a sad letter, it must be given to my beloved.  
3. He wrote a short but sad letter, in which he says farewell to his beloved, why does cruel fate forbid our love, that you may never be mine.  
4. And I, sad, unfortunate, do not know where the cold waves will carry me, whether they will throw me onto the shore or carry me further and further away.  
5. When I shall rest in the cold grave, let a beautiful forget-me-not be planted, in memory of our faithful love, that I had a faithful beloved.  
6. When I shall rot in the cold grave, offer the Our Father for me there, in memory of our faithful love, that I was your faithful lover.', '1. I shed tears for you, that you do not love me, I carry sorrow in my heart that you are distancing yourself from me.  
2. The sun has stopped shining, your love has ceased, I must not ask for your hand, it is already promised to another.  
3. The days have passed, those I longed for, gone are the beautiful dreams in which I found bliss.  
4. Oh, away and away with everything, away is my hope, now I weep like a child, what good will it do me?  
5. You are not moved, your heart is stone, it drives me to despair, it torments my heart.  
6. If only you knew a little of the pain in my heart, surely you would forever banish your cruelty.  
7. But you constantly seek a reason to part, and you won’t even see me to my grief.  
8. No one loved you as faithfully as I did, you were my heaven, this I saw myself.  
9. I thought of you by day, also by night, I sought help from you in my suffering.  
10. So farewell now, remember me too, I say for the last time that my promise was not a lie.  
11. Be happy in this world, enjoy your joys, if happiness blooms for you, I am without sorrow.', "1. The crib is made, the patient lies in it, three doctors stand by her, treating her illness.  
2. Then one of the three doctors shrugged his shoulders, you're a lovesick virgin, there is no help for you.  
3. Send a black coffin here, lay me into it, place my slender white body inside it.  
4. Fetch my lover for me, my darling, so he may come to visit his patient.  
5. Oh, my dear patient, your lover spoils you, to make you give him peace, that he does not love you.  
6. Send me a painter, I will have him paint me, so when my heart aches, I can look at him.  
7. Oh, my dear patient, your painter sends word that he says today is a great holiday, that he will not paint today.  
8. Give me large candles here, place them by my head, my black shiny hair, brush it for me.  
9. And in that one moment, the doors flew open, step back, you three doctors, nothing hurts me anymore."]

Name: 17_repeated_iya_eya_fashion
Representative_Docs:
['Whose heart glows for purest pleasure,  
Seeks a dear wife,  
To whom he is steadfastly bound,  
By pure love and loyalty;  
He searches with a joyful mind,  
For an object worthy of him,  
For nothing on earth is as sweet,  
As truly being paired. (repeat)  
Rejoice then, the loving pair,  
Who heart to heart unite,  
And let the cups ring together,  
For Groom and Bride!  
This hour, which fulfills our wish,  
Is truly worth a festive toast,  
For nothing on earth is as sweet,  
As truly being paired. (repeat)  
Live, Groom! live in love and joy,  
With the Bride your friend,  
Who joyfully delights your heart  
In the blessing of marital love;  
Make sure a year soon comes to an end,  
That you also gather something young,  
For such fruits are certainly sweet,  
For those who pair in joy. (repeat)  
Flourish for the welfare of your existence,  
Prosperity above all,  
May your true lineage endure,  
By countless little shoots;  
So may a joyful procession play  
Of offspring worthy of you,  
And the heart tells you, nothing is so sweet,  
As truly being paired. (repeat)', 'Come here, lovers of stockings,
Do not pass by my shop,
Here is for Turks, Jews, and Gypsies:
For burghers, farmers, or dandy,
My stall is well stocked,
Whatever a count or noble desires;
No countryman can come here,
Whether he pretends any color,
Whether single or double-layered:
No matter how he might dream it.
If you seek a decent little stocking,
Pleuntje will please you,
Step freely into my shop, brave one,
Here are both soft and stiff:
Here they are very finely picked,
Darned, embroidered, and fringed;
Entirely rough and also very smooth,
For Germans or French, Moors or Scotch
Who ride on horseback or go on foot;
For Scots and for Walloons.
No color on earth is to be named,
Or is obtainable here,
Do not pass by my shop briskly:
But step in without hesitation;
Ash gray, bright blue, and thunder green,
That I have in the newest fashion,
Pure white, also red, and gray,
I have them open with a hole,
Whether elongated, round, or flat,
For fools and for wise men.
My stockings just made with stitch and needle,
With buttons according to fashion,
For boatmen or for soldiers,
Whoever needs them,
Look at the color, look at the thread,
See inside the leg, how fine the seam:
Where one can aspire,
Step in, gentlemen, here you have it all,
Do you want wide, narrow, broad, or slim?
Pleuntje is waiting for you.', 'Come, let us raise our glasses once more,

For Groom and Bride; repeated.  
But quietly, the time has improved,

Congratulations on your wedding celebration,  
Good luck, oh young Man and Woman!  
Come, let us clink glasses once more, repeated.  
All that we wished for you was sincere,  
And it was good for us, gathered here together,  
To drink to your well-being. repeated.  
However harsh nature may appear,  
Oh friends! never forget this,  
Every season brings flowers; repeated.  

I have only this youthful Couple,  
Our joyful gathering together,  
To name as proof for you. repeated.  
Beloved ones! then step into the boat,  
With pure faithfulness and marital love,  
You have no storm to fear, repeated.

Whatever the eye may see. repeated.  
Even if sometimes it blows a bit,  
So that the boat turns around,  
You have nothing to dread; repeated.  
If pure love and faithfulness are at the helm,  
Whoever has ever sailed in their company,  
Has always fared well. repeated.']

Name: 18_palm_good woman_new years_new year
Representative_Docs:
['We come here with our star,  
we seek Lord Jesus, we wished so much.  
We already came to Herod’s door,  
Herod the king himself came out.  
Herod the king spoke with a false heart:  
“How is the youngest of the three so dark?”  
Though he is somewhat dark, he is well known, he is the youngest from the Orient,  
He is the youngest from foreign lands,  
where all those stars burn so quietly.  
Well star, stand still and do not move anymore,  
it is a sign from God the Lord.  
Well star, you must not stand so quietly,  
you must go with us to Bethlehem,  
To Bethlehem, that beautiful city,  
where Mary sat with her little child.  
The smaller the child, the greater the God,  
whom all the Jews have mocked.  
We have already sung before this house,  
give us the coin with a good cross!  
Though it is no cross, let it be a coin,  
give us the coin that you grant us!', 'I.
Enough of idle reasoning,
That’s good for one who has eaten.
Now let us jingle a little tune,
That sticks to our ribs:
Drink once, it’s welcome,
No matter how much is brought to me.
I believe most poets fart with Apollo;
For none of them ever thought of drinking.

II.
The first shouts at us his head full of his desire;
Likewise; as if there were yet some mystery in it.
I prefer Bruno, who sang like a bard;
And ended each rhyme with a glass,
It’s fine amusement to hang his own business on the clock.
I used to get a lesson to keep silent;
Or else I was the scapegoat the next day.

III.
The second is struck in reason,
Who bluffs and enjoys Dullemans’ music;
And sings of things we do not ask about,
Of Pook, Stopmes, Cortelas and Piek;
Yes, he sings freely so that one hears
What you know of Wintbuyls,
Of knights, and of lances with all their circumstances;
Sing, for here stands no madhouse only about.

IV.
This one was worth being laughed at with farts;
Because here he spoils wounds from his garden.
It seems a paradise for those who do not know it;
But more fertile than Pier Wouter’s dune.
Here a tree bears cheese, milk, and cream,
Wine, beer, bread, meat, and fish.
Where else would one find a linden, covered with lindens,
Which is so rich, with various fruits!

V.
This one had to go live by a miller;
There the turning always comes in handy:
Where he points Saint Vechter to his crown,
Who sometimes grinds; and not half so fast.
He turns me blind with all his wind,
Makes my head confused.
It seems to me this spectacle vendor
Sat better and more comfortably,
Where the spectacles are the gable of the house.

VI.
Among all these crazy people raised,
Only the last speaks with reason;
Who likes a lot to lick spoons,
And to storm with knife and fork in hand.
Broth and pap is too weak for him;
That costs spooners;
He prefers turkeys
To kiss belly and anus:
And the fall of crowned storks.

VII.
Long live here a fresh glass, or a beaker;
It’s wine but all that is said;
The health of the apothecary,
Who today bravely stokes the white turf:
Well, now it sounds pretty out;
And if there is anyone,
Who finds a drop in it;
Beat me with a club,
That I out of fear again fill such a glass with piss.

VIII.
Now I also join in the refrains;
For whoever wants, it does not matter to me,
Think that I want to sit alone,
As if I were a jester or a sultan?
No, certainly not! That would be sadness:
I have consumed too much
With worthies and students,
And all those lively people,
Who lubricate more than wagon wheels.

IX.
The poems are a recreation;
They once make people’s hearts glad:
And shorten the already long span
Of the old unpleasant times;
Whether sonnet or ballet;
Or stately madrigal,
Or klinkers, or rondeels,
Or gentle table plays,
So long as it is in pure German tongue.

X.
Long live, long live our Signor Franciscus
Who often has delighted us,
That no panther beast, nor basilisk
Drag him to the grave before his due time.
His wine and tarts are ripe in March;
And that is our harvest;
Wherein we eagerly soak
Much more than the churches:
So that with us neither throat nor knife rusts.', "1.
